query: W melts near 3422 °C, whereas Cu boils near 2562 °C, so conventional induction or arc-plasma casting cannot readily yield a uniform W–Cu material. Phase separation and void formation can impair thermal transport. Filling a W skeleton with molten Cu or Cu powder can leave defects; spark-plasma sintering and mechanical alloying can produce finer, more uniform structures but can also leave voids; vapor-coated W powders have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between the constituents; and metal 3D printing has also been explored. Starting from W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix for heat transfer under irradiation in fusion-reactor joints, what single intervention could overcome these limitations while preserving mechanical durability? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts an outcome relative to a named existing fabrication baseline, defines the processing and service boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment and observations that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Using a novel hybrid additive manufacturing and spark-plasma sintering process can produce a uniform W-Cu composite material with enhanced thermal transport properties and preserved mechanical durability.
generation.material_initial_state: Tungsten (W) particles or connected W regions within a Copper (Cu) matrix
generation.intervention: Hybrid additive manufacturing and spark-plasma sintering process
generation.conditions: High-temperature and high-pressure conditions during spark-plasma sintering
generation.structural_mediator: Uniform dispersion of W particles within the Cu matrix
generation.mechanism: Enhanced thermal transport due to improved interface contact between W and Cu, and reduced void formation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved thermal conductivity and mechanical durability compared to conventional casting or sintering methods
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the optimal processing parameters for the hybrid additive manufacturing and spark-plasma sintering process

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled comparative study of thermal conductivity and mechanical durability
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the hybrid additive manufacturing and spark-plasma sintering process does not produce a significant improvement in thermal conductivity and mechanical durability compared to the conventional casting or sintering methods, the hypothesis is falsified.
